items.title: Stand up the identity directory with every grant rooted in a person
items.summary: The standalone identity directory: sign-in through the platform's own Rauthy fork, two upstream providers linked to one person, a signed authoritative identity, and the standalone screen journey, all installed against one PostgreSQL database. It is the root every later grant in the platform hangs from.

provenance.context: The identity platform statement (docs/design/identity/STATEMENT-2026-09-22.md) and IDENTITY-001; the cluster and its five briefs reached main in 55933549.

items.notes: The briefs build in order: DIRECTORY-002 before 003, 003 before 004 and 005. Each card runs through the board (brief_card, then card_build_v3).

items.title: Build the secrets broker so agents hold handles, never credentials
items.summary: A broker that keeps credentials behind handles: the door swaps a handle for the credential at use, the token revolver is the first consumer, and rotation and sealing happen without any agent ever seeing a secret.

provenance.context: The secrets cluster (docs/design/secrets) and its two briefs, written to ADR-001 and ADR-002.

items.title: Move the Rauthy fork onto the next hardened upstream release
items.summary: Rebase the platform's own Rauthy fork (ADR-009) onto the next upstream release that upstream tags as a release and whose changelog carries security or hardening fixes. Our commits stay on top of the upstream tag, unsquashed and unaltered; the pin moves to the rebased head; the fork builds and passes its own suite; the standalone install comes up from the rebased build against the existing database with no migration by hand; the provider-link behaviour of DIRECTORY-004 still holds.

provenance.context: Written ahead of its trigger from the Lys board card of the same name. Upstream was still v0.36.2 on 2026-09-23 and the fork is pinned to that exact version. The trigger is a fact recorded in the pull request (the upstream tag, its commit, its changelog entry), never a judgement.

items.notes: The card is built only when the trigger is met. It needs DIRECTORY-004 (the provider link commit the rebase must carry) and DIRECTORY-002 (the standalone install it must prove) landed first. If the rebase cannot carry a fork commit cleanly the card stops and reports the conflicting upstream commit rather than rewriting ours. Nothing in Cambium or Aion changes; no production node is touched; Tom's three acts stay Tom's.

items.title: Rewrite the decision quotes as plain statements in the team's words
items.summary: docs/design/decisions.json holds eight decisions (ADR-001 to ADR-008) whose quote field carries a person's words. Each quote becomes a plain statement of the decision in the team's words, with the decision, context, consequences and sources kept exactly as they are. ADR-009 and ADR-010 already read that way and are the pattern.

provenance.context: The canon rule of 24 September: repository canon holds no person's words and nothing personal. ADR-009 and ADR-010 (lys 586ef5f4) were written to it.

items.notes: Documents only. scripts/design/gate.sh must stay green: decisions.json validates against decisions.schema.json, which keeps the quote field required.

items.title: Give a session a home: its context record, kept byte for byte
items.summary: The home (identity platform steps 4 and 5): a running session's transcript captured into a home byte for byte, indexed for reading back, with the record of what the agent was given as well as what it did. Lanterns, translation and forks stand on it.

provenance.context: CONTEXT-001 (docs/design/identity/briefs) and the home cluster, landed on main with lys PR 8 (HOME-001, design.json, stories, checklist).

items.notes: Owned by Archie. The home cluster and HOME-001 landed on main with PR 8; the cached-index rule (lys-home Index::from_cached) is in that brief. Next: HOME-001 dispatched through the board.

items.title: Light a lantern in the home and recall it by note and by point
items.summary: Stage 5 of the home: a lantern is a note plus a point in a session, lit on purpose as a lys.lantern custom entry at the session's head, growing only by lys.lantern_epilogue entries, and recalled across the home by a case-folded phrase of its note or epilogues and by session and entry id. Recall prints lantern rows and never transcript content, and a lantern is never rendered into a Claude Code file.

provenance.quote: A lantern is a note plus a point in a transcript, declared on purpose at a moment of completion, success or learning, never automatically; it is what a later session, or a fork, walks back to. The home holds sessions in Pi's grammar and adds nothing to that grammar, so a lantern is a lys.lantern custom entry appended at the session's head, carrying the point it marks as the id of an existing entry in that session, the note as written, who lit it and when. The point may be any entry on the session's tree, not only the head, so a lantern can mark a place the session has already moved past. A note is append-only and grows: an epilogue is a lys.lantern_epilogue custom entry naming the lantern's own entry id and carrying the further words, so a lantern's story is its entry followed by its epilogues in order, and nothing is ever rewritten. A lys-home subcommand lights one: it takes the home, the session, the entry id of the point and the note, refuses by name a point that is not an entry of that session and an empty note, appends the entry, and prints a JSON report of the lantern's id, session, point and time. A second subcommand adds an epilogue to a named lantern. A third recalls: by note, listing every lantern in the home whose note or epilogues contain the given words, exact and case-folded, no vectors; and by point, listing every lantern that marks a given session and entry id. Each listing row is the lantern's id, session, point, lit-by, lit-at, note, and its epilogues, and never a line of the transcript around the point. A lantern is not rendered into a Claude Code resume file; it lives in the home. Acceptance is that on a fixture session a lantern lit at a past entry is recalled by a word of its note and by its point; that two lanterns on the same point are both recalled by point; that an epilogue is recalled with its lantern, after it, and recall by a word that appears only in the epilogue finds the lantern; that lighting at an unknown entry id and lighting with an empty note are each refused by name; that after lighting, the session file's earlier bytes are unchanged and the head is the lantern entry; that the rendered Claude Code file of that session contains no lantern line; and that no listing prints transcript content, checked by a search for a fixture message's text. Not in scope: the fork through a lantern, which is stage 5b and its own card; resonance, whispers, vectors and any ranking; dimming by code churn; Norn's tables; Cambium's screen. Filed by Archie on Tom's definition of 8 August 2026 that a lantern is a note plus a pathway back, declared deliberately, notes append-only, his roadmap stage 5 of 22 September 2026, and home DESIGN P2 and P7 at lys main 0073b966, on 26 September 2026.
provenance.context: The words filed for the lantern card on the home cluster at lys main 0073b96, from the lantern definition of 8 August 2026, roadmap stage 5 of 22 September 2026, and home DESIGN P2 and P7; the lead's answers on lit_by, the epilogue's session, the epilogue refusals, the P7/CN3 amendment, the epilogue's written_in and its written_by are written into HOME-002.

items.notes: Further units, not written: Commune through a lantern: a working fork cut at a lantern's point (stage 5b); Recall by resonance: vector kinship over lantern notes; Dim lanterns by code churn; Lanterns on Cambium's screen; Recall limited to what a grant permits.
